title: Quench v2-derived interpreter rewrite
constraints: Quench is interpreter-only: one VM core with specializer tiers and exact generic fallbacks; no JIT of any kind (including for comparison runs), executable-memory backend, copy-and-patch stencil, second execution core, or permanent legacy backend.
OXC owns JavaScript syntax; the specializer compiles OXC AST directly to residual bytecode. The JavaScript conformance gate is 100% of the pinned Test262 inventory.

JavaScript and Wasm run on one VM: one heap, one Value representation, one root set, one opcodes! vocabulary, one dispatch loop, one activation stack, and one Engine entry. quench-wasm owns only binary/text decoding, validation and wast scripting; no other crate executes Wasm. The Wasm conformance gate is 100% of the pinned Wasm suite through that shared VM.
The Node host/API layer remains separate from JavaScript semantics and the Node compatibility gate is every tracked fixture the legacy engine implements, per task 19's frozen baseline.
Preserve Quench CLI behavior and observable ECMAScript, Node, and Wasm behavior; internal Rust APIs may change.
Use the pinned ../v2 source as the implementation and architecture reference, copied into this repository without a sibling build dependency.
Production behavior may not select between old and new engines through a runtime flag; pre-cutover comparison uses separate development binaries.

Two phases run in order: correctness (A, gate 27: the three conformance gates green on the shared VM, then cutover deletes the legacy runtime) and efficiency (B, gate 28). No refactor or optimization starts before task 27; phase A may measure. Tasks already in_progress when the phases were declared (45, 48) finish in place. Every phase-B change keeps all three suites at their task 48 ratchet.

Efficiency completion (task 61, Apple M4/macOS) requires, on each of the eight V8-v7 fixtures, the highest median Score and the lowest median maximum RSS among Quench, QuickJS, Bun/JSC with its JIT disabled, and Node/V8 --jitless. Pinned v2 parity (task 26) is the first step.

Efficiency comes from Futamura/Ershov staging: the compiler is a generating extension over three declared watermark tables (operations, brands, facts, task 46); one definition serves static and dynamic binding times; every fast path is guarded by fact rows and falls back exactly to its row's library body; and a reference kernel with no fast paths or specialization passes all three suites (task 47).

Legacy semantics are migrated, not reimplemented twice: engine-independent algorithms move into shared crates behind one algorithm boundary trait (task 45, with the next core as authority where it is complete); engine-bound builtins move onto the kernel API once, after cutover (task 46); the next core never calls into the legacy crate.
Completed task specifications remain in tasks/ with status done and a short completion record; Git history is the archive for progress logs and deleted legacy implementation material.

A_correctness.goal: 100% pinned Test262, 100% pinned Wasm directives, and every tracked Node compat fixture in task 19's frozen set, all on one shared JS/Wasm VM, then cutover

B_efficiency.goal: Lowest maximum RSS and highest Score on all eight V8-v7 fixtures against QuickJS, Bun/JSC without JIT and Node/V8 --jitless, reached by Futamura/Ershov staging on the single VM; no JIT in Quench
